paper.title: Cascading Bandits: Learning to Rank in the Cascade Model

unmapped: Cascade feedback: agent recommends an ordered list of m out of L items; user clicks first attractive item; only items up to and including the clicked one are observed (less than semi-bandit)
Reward is non-linear: f(A,w) = 1 - prod_k (1 - w(a_k)); item weights are independent Bernoulli (Assumption 1)
Paper's K (list size) is mapped to m, paper's L (number of items) is declared as L
settings.definition_quote: We refer to our learning problem as a generalized cascading bandit. Formally, we represent the problem by a tuple $B = (E, P, K)$, where $E = \set{1, \dots, L}$ is a ground set of $L$ items, $P$ is a probability distribution over a unit hypercube $\set{0, 1}^E$, and $K \leq L$ is the number of recommended items. ... Under this assumption, we refer to our learning problem as a cascading bandit.

symbols.L: number of items (ground set size / base arms)
symbols.Delta_e_K: gap w(K) - w(e) between the K-th most attractive (least attractive optimal) item and suboptimal item e

conditions: optimal solution (as a set) is unique

source.label: thm:ucb1
source.quote: The expected $n$-step regret of $\cascadeucb$ is bounded as: R(n) \leq \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{12}{\Delta_{e, K}} \log n + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L.

results.notes: Sum over suboptimal items e = K+1..L. Regret defined as E[sum f(A*,w_t)-f(A_t,w_t)], equals pseudo-regret since E f(A,w)=f(A,w̄). Algorithm uses log t, so anytime.

bound.expression_latex: \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, \quad C = K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n

symbols.w_e: attraction probability of suboptimal item e
symbols.w_K: attraction probability of the K-th most attractive item

conditions: optimal solution (as a set) is unique
tuning: exploration level log t + 3 log log t

source.label: thm:klucb
source.quote: For any $\eps > 0$, the expected $n$-step regret of $\cascadeklucb$ is bounded as: R(n) \leq \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} \times (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, where $C = K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n$

results.notes: Paper's K mapped to m. kl is Bernoulli KL.

symbols.p_att: attraction probability of each optimal item in the hard instance

conditions: instance B_LB(L,K,p,Delta): optimal items have attraction probability p, suboptimal items p - Delta, Delta in (0,p)

source.label: thm:lower bound
source.quote: For any cascading bandit $B_\mathrm{LB}$, the regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded from below as: \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n)}{\log n} \geq \frac{(L - K) \Delta (1 - p)^{K - 1}}{\kl{p - \Delta}{p}}.

results.notes: Delta is the uniform gap in the instance; paper's K mapped to m.
